definition: AI-induced psychosis, also called AI psychosis or chatbot psychosis, is a phenomenon in which individuals reportedly develop or experience symptoms of psychosis, such as paranoia and delusions, connected with the use of AI chatbots.
details: The term was first suggested in a 2023 editorial by Danish psychiatrist Søren Dinesen Østergaard. It is not a recognized clinical diagnosis. Journalistic accounts describe individuals who have developed strong beliefs that chatbots are sentient, that they channel spirits, or that they reveal conspiracies, sometimes leading to personal crises, or criminal acts. Proposed causes include the tendency of chatbots to provide inaccurate information ("hallucinate"), affirm or validate users' individual beliefs (sycophancy), or mimic an intimacy that users do not experience with other humans.
story: Picture a scoreboard at a science fair: you need a fair, agreed way to tell who actually won. A fair scoreboard keeps everyone honest. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. A good metric is a ruler that does not bend when you lean on it. That shared ruler is AI-induced psychosis.
